It is clear that some of the same gods claim to be skilled in medicine, others are most excellent sophists and excel in eloquence, some teach others and are skilled in homicide and cruelty, others are knowledgeable in base arts and are inventors of evil things, each one is suited to the nature that is attributed to them, but how can such gods exist, who can say that a god is one who is destitute of some good, when they have an abundance of all things and are most powerful and perfect

Someone will say, for what reason, excellent man, if truly they have been endowed with the highest nature, and God is the son of Coronis, not healing everyone, and thus, oh noble one, it seems to me that they have their own powerful nature, and the truth is that not all are approved, but each has their own peculiar virtue, healing and adding their own art, and some exhibit their own specimen, and they have their own nature, and some work in part, and others make their own experience, and some have their own erudition, and others have eloquence and war experience, and some have a trade, and others are craftsmen, and some are wise, and human nature is superior to their studies, and the teachers of arts and sciences are numerous and excellent

If it can happen that some people know the art of speaking truth, and are better than others, and have medical and war knowledge like the Greeks, and few of us have this, and if someone has a chance to be a doctor and eloquent and have praise for other arts, and is famous, then our minds are to be blamed, and we are only able to do one thing, and it is not shameful to be ignorant about some things, but in one person, all these gifts are gathered, and how can we not be amazed, and Julian says something else, that we have a natural ability, and we can do something, and we can overcome the foolishness of the Greeks, and their religion is not as good as the Christian religion, and they have some good things, like doctors, and then he says that the Greeks are better, and he writes this, so should he not be ashamed

Sculptors will demonstrate that gods exist, who are not known, and they are unclean demons, or rather, corrupt men have approved them, and they are said to be gods, but they are not, and they have been struck, as we said before, and perhaps no Christian is skilled in medicine or eloquence or war, and it is necessary to establish the gods who have invented and taught, and there are many things in life, and it is necessary to know the reasons for all things, even the most insignificant

Julian says that since he was sick, many things in the matter were suggested to him by Jupiter, and the ways of medical treatments were introduced to him, and he wonders if the wise mind, which sees all the doctrines of the Greeks, is ignorant of the art, and he admires Asclepius, who, as if dictating, suggests a remedy while sitting in a chair, and he asks what God should do, liberate from diseases or suggest remedies, and he questions whether Asclepius, knowing the art, suggested the remedy or if it is more proper for God to heal the sick

How we, having moderate knowledge, are to depart from weaknesses, worshiping one true God, and from Him given human wisdom, prudence, and every use of reason, and honest things, and He orders to destroy weaknesses, and someone saying gods are those having human skills, and having experience, and we confess God as maker, author, and giver of goods, but Julianus strays from truth, and we, on the other hand, do not err, when we attribute skills to Mars, Vulcan, and Muses, and eloquent ones…
pass_b_english: ...It is evident, therefore, that of the same gods, some are skilled in medicine, others are most excellent sophists and excel in eloquence, some teach others and are skilled in homicide and cruelty, others are knowledgeable in base arts and are inventors of evil things.
Each one is suited to the nature that is attributed to them.

Someone will say, for what reason, excellent man, if truly they have been endowed with the highest nature, and God is the son of Coronis, not healing everyone (Isaiah 29:13), and thus, oh noble one, it seems to me that they have their own powerful nature, and the truth is that not all are approved, but each has their own peculiar virtue, healing and adding their own art, and some exhibit their own specimen, and they have their own nature, and some work in part, and some make their own experience, and some have their own erudition, and some have eloquence and war experience, and some have a trade, and some are craftsmen, and some are wise, and human nature is superior to their studies, and the teachers of arts and sciences are numerous and excellent.

If it can happen that some people know the art of speaking truth, surpassing others in this regard, and have medical and war knowledge like the Greeks, and few of us have this, and if someone has a chance to be a doctor and eloquent and have praise for other arts, and is famous, then our minds are to be blamed, and we are only able to do one thing, and it is not shameful to be ignorant of certain matters.
In reality, all these gifts are combined in one person, and it is astonishing to behold.
Julian proposes another idea, suggesting that we have a natural ability that enables us to achieve something and overcome the foolishness of the Greeks.

He claims that their religion is inferior to the Christian faith, yet they do possess some admirable qualities, such as skilled doctors, but nevertheless, he asserts that the Greeks are superior, and he commits this statement to writing, which is a cause for shame.

The sculptors will demonstrate that the gods they worship are not truly known, but rather they are unclean spirits or corrupt men who have been approved by the people, and these so-called gods are said to have the power to heal in a manner worthy of God, but they are not truly divine.
Perhaps no Christian is skilled in the arts of medicine or eloquence or war.

Julian claims that since he was sick, many things in the matter were suggested to him by Jupiter, and the ways of medical treatments were introduced to him, and he wonders if the wise mind, which sees all the doctrines of the Greeks, might be ignorant of the art of healing, and he wonders if it is more proper for God to set people free from diseases or to suggest remedies.

He admires Asclepius, who, as if suggesting, suggests a remedy while sitting in a chair, and Julian wonders whether Asclepius, knowing the art, suggested the remedy or if it is more proper for God to heal the sick.

We, who possess moderate knowledge, are to set free from weaknesses, worshiping the one true God, and from Him given human wisdom, prudence, and every use of reason, and honest things, and He orders to destroy weaknesses, and someone saying gods are those having human skills, and having experience, and we confess God as maker, author, and giver of goods, but Julianus strays from truth, and we, on the other hand, do not err, when we attribute skills to Mars, Vulcan, and Muses, and eloquent ones.
It is necessary to know the reasons for all things, even the most insignificant aspects of life and study.
